claims.text: W, Mo, Ta, Nb, and V are described collectively as Group IV-V transition metals.
Mixed elemental or gas-atomized refractory-metal powders typically contain high levels of C, N, and O interstitial impurities.
Equiatomic W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V can be fabricated by LPBF through in-situ alloying of mixed elemental powders.
Favorable LPBF parameters can completely fuse the W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles.
A linear energy density of approximately 2.83 J/mm is suitable for complete fusion of the proposed W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloy.
The proposed LPBF parameters will produce 99.8% relative density.
A multi-step aging treatment can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in LPBF-produced W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V.
Vacuum or inert-atmosphere heat treatment will control interstitial content and preserve precipitate coherency.
The desired SCCP microstructure consists of discrete coherent B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent SCCP interfaces relieve stress concentrations that would otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
Coherent SCCP interfaces simultaneously act as strengthening barriers and permit dislocation transmission.
An inverted BCC+B2 structure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix improves room-temperature ductility while retaining high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures.
The SCCP microstructure will mitigate brittleness caused specifically by C, N, and O interstitial impurities.
The treated W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloy will achieve tensile strength above 2.15 GPa and approximately 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The treated W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloy will retain a yield strength of approximately 1.05 GPa at 800 °C.
The alloy will retain ductility above 10% at temperatures up to 800 °C.
Continuous ordered B2 matrices in conventional two-phase refractory HEAs cause poor room-temperature ductility.
LPBF refractory alloys with dendritic or cellular microstructures lacking coherent precipitates exhibit high strength but low ductility.
The resulting alloy will show no significant property loss from interstitial embrittlement.

contradictions.description: The desired mediator is explicitly a set of discrete B2 precipitates, but the falsification rule says that finding discontinuous precipitates would falsify the hypothesis. A discrete precipitate phase is ordinarily discontinuous, so the success criterion and falsification criterion conflict.
